label: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017
output:
Kristen,

Here's the straight story. No excuses — it was my popcorn.

Saturday, Nov. 7, around 10:40, I put a bag in the break room microwave and hit the popcorn button. Then I went out front. A customer needed a shear pin for his snowblower, and it took longer than I figured, maybe six or seven minutes. By the time I got back it had already gone off. Store was cleared out about 25 minutes. The engine came from Hertel. No damage, just smoke and stink.

The September alarm was not me — that was the sensor in the paint aisle. But this one is on me, not the microwave. Thirty-one years on the job, and I get my first alarm as a civilian over a bag of butter popcorn. Mikey Szymanski was on the engine. I broke him in as a probie back in '03, and he will never let me forget this. My wife said the van smelled like a burnt movie theater.

I feel bad about the Hendersons leaving a full cart. They'll be back, they always are, but I still feel bad. I'm sorry for putting everybody out in the cold, and sorry for the extra headache with Gary and the insurance people.

The $175 is on me. Take it out of my check or I'll bring cash, your call. Put Denise's coffee on me too.

Please keep me on Saturdays. I like the weekend crowd, and I need the hours for heating oil. I'll stay clear of the microwave.

Walt
